topic: The doorway effect: why you forget why you walked into a room
title: Why You Forget Things Walking Into a Room
voiceover: Why do you forget why you walked into this room? In 2011, Gabriel Radvansky's team studied students moving through real and virtual rooms. People forgot more after walking through a doorway than after walking the same distance within one room. The researchers proposed that a doorway creates a new memory episode, an event boundary, making the old information harder to retrieve. But in 2021, Jessica McFadyen and colleagues ran four experiments across virtual reality, video and real-life movement. They found no significant effect of doorways on forgetting. Only when people had to hold information in mind did doorways increase certain memory errors. So the doorway effect looks real in some conditions, but not guaranteed. So if you blank in a doorway, it's a documented memory quirk studied in healthy students. Tomorrow: why does something you just learned seem to appear everywhere?

description: Does walking through a doorway really make you forget? A 2011 study found people forgot more after passing through a door, but a 2021 set of experiments mostly did not find a clean effect. New psychology short every day on The Psyche Discourse. Source: Radvansky, G. A., Krawietz, S. A., & Tamplin, A. K. (2011). Walking through doorways causes forgetting: Further explorations. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, 64(8), 1632-1645. Source: McFadyen, J., Nolan, C., Pinocy, E., Buteri, D., & Baumann, O. (2021). Doorways do not always cause forgetting: A multimodal investigation. BMC Psychology, 9.
accuracy_note: CONTESTED / MIXED. Radvansky et al. (2011) found the effect in real and virtual rooms; McFadyen et al. (2021) found no significant overall effect across four experiments, only increased memory errors under a working-memory load. No 'fix' is claimed, because later research found the effect even after returning to the original room (not claimed here for lack of a single verified primary source).
